name: restic-deterministic-provider-native-bulk-removal
instr:
restic cannot deterministically reconcile every requested object after bulk removal succeeds, partially fails, or is cancelled. Implement provider-native bulk removal that reduces overhead without changing deletion, prune, index replacement, or dry-run behavior.

Report exactly one input-ordered outcome per request, preserving duplicates and completed outcomes while distinguishing success, failure, and unattempted work. Azure, B2, GCS, local, memory, REST, S3, SFTP, and Swift must preserve normalization, missing-object, error-classification, and deletion semantics. Bound provider-native concurrency by configured connection allowances and keep mutable state concurrency-safe. azure.Create, b2.Create, and gs.Create must still supply concrete Backends.

Preserve handle identity in grouped and out-of-order responses. Never fabricate success from malformed or partial responses. REST must drain responses and support servers without batching. Retry only eligible failures without repeating confirmed deletions. Cache only evicts confirmed removals; dry-run suppresses mutation; mocks allow deterministic outcomes. Preserve result identity through retry, repository translation, parallel reporting, index cleanup, and prune. Count only confirmed removals while preserving callback sequencing, phase order, messages, warnings, strict and best-effort policies, dry-run plans, and terminal results.
